originality.rationale: Live retrieval shows no prior (5,2) census, diameters, or paired witnesses. arXiv API quiver+census 0 hits, exchange+graph+diameter+quiver 0 hits; Crossref five-vertex census top-5 are Auslander-Reiten/quiver-representation hits in different domain, none is cluster-mutation census. JEMS DOI confirms 11 exceptionals E6,E7,E8,tilde E, E^{(1,1)}, X6,X7. No existing table gives F, canonical 5x5 reps, labeled orders/diameters (270,7),(600,8),(720,9),(1440,11),(1680,11),(1980,11),(2184,11), or replayable closure/growth logs. Stratum choice is theoretically forced (bound 2 saturated for rank>=3 finite mutation, rank 5 largest exceptional-free, rank 6 with 5^15~30B infeasible), not mere n->n+1 substitution.

value.rationale: Result is independently worth finding later. It closes a real gap between textbook rank-2/3 Markov dynamics and wild FST classification by delivering the first complete enumerative instantiation to the saturated exceptional-free stratum: exact F=7 with lex-min representatives, labeled orders and diameters (new structural data), fully closed D5 witness with per-node paths and adjacency, and 12-step unbounded witness 2->1.6e62 with preserved C=5 plus induction proof. Provides citable benchmark for cluster-algebra software (Sage, Keller explorer) and Seiberg-duality quiver work where small quivers are test cases. Not a textbook restatement (D5/Markov are only witnesses among 7, full census with diameters/logs required), not parameter substitution (threshold argument documented), not tiny gain (no prior table, first catalog), not unexplained enumeration (invariant pre-filter rationale, diameter datum, paired finite-closed vs unbounded-growth witnesses with Markov monotonicity, independent recheck in <2min stdlib+numpy). Fallback bounds not needed; full census achieved. Limitations honestly flagged (surface tilings conjectural, orders/diameters machine-checked).
